successCriteria.description: NotificationStatus is defined locally in the notification model file as a type alias exposing exactly the values PENDING, SENT, READ, and ARCHIVED — not imported from shared types.

The Notification entity omits an updatedAt field entirely, distinguishing it from Employee/Policy/Leave/Balance which all carry updatedAt — matching the notifications table schema that has no updated_at column.

The repository interface declares all four operations: findByRecipientId, create, markAsRead, and updateStatus — each returning the correct Promise type (array, entity, nullable entity, nullable entity respectively).
findByRecipientId returns notifications for the given recipient ordered by creation time descending, and returns an empty array when no rows match.

create persists a notification row and returns the mapped entity; the input type excludes id, createdAt, and readAt (auto-generated/null), and the insert lets the database generate id and created_at while read_at defaults to null.
markAsRead atomically sets both read_at to the current timestamp and status to READ in a single UPDATE, returning the updated entity or null when no row matches the id.
updateStatus performs a generic status transition to any NotificationStatus value, returning the updated entity or null when no row matches the id.
The repository's row mapper converts snake_case database columns to camelCase entity fields, constructs Date objects for created_at, and maps a null read_at to null (not undefined) on the entity.

The barrel export re-exports the Notification entity, NotificationStatus type, INotificationRepository interface, and NotificationRepository concrete class so the module is consumable via its public entry point.
Unit tests mock the shared db connection pool and assert exact SQL strings and exact parameter arrays for each repository method, covering found/not-found/empty cases and nullable read_at mapping.

The implementation compiles under strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) with no use of the any type — the row mapper parameter is typed as Record<string, unknown> with explicit casts.

constraints: All database access goes through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository) — the NotificationRepository is the only component that executes SQL against the notifications table.
No use of the any type (no-any harness rule, severity high) — use unknown with type guards or explicit casts instead; the row mapper must type its parameter as Record<string, unknown>.
All SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) — never interpolate values into the query string (SQL injection prevention).
The repository must import the pg pool from the shared db connection module via the established relative path, not instantiate its own Pool or manage connections directly.
Modules import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts) — no cross-module imports of another module's internal files.
No unhandled promise rejections (GP-006) — async repository methods must not let errors from pool.query propagate unhandled beyond their own catch/return boundary.
outOfScope: Notification service (INotificationService / NotificationService) — the reconciled architecture lists it as owned by the notification module, but this phase scope covers only the model, repository, and barrel export.
Notification controller and routes — no HTTP layer is created in this phase; the leave service (Phase 9) and routes (Phase 10) will consume the repository.
Database migrations / CREATE TABLE DDL for the notifications table — the code agent generates migrations separately; this phase defines the entity and repository against the conceptual schema.
Audit logging for notification state changes (GP-002) — the audit module does not yet exist (Phase 7); notification lifecycle auditing is deferred to the leave service orchestration phase.
RBAC enforcement on notification access (GP-005) — no API endpoints exist in this phase; access control is applied at the controller/middleware layer in a later phase.
Input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) — no API boundary exists in this phase; validation is deferred to the controller layer.

entityInvariants.invariant: The Notification lifecycle progresses PENDING → SENT → READ → ARCHIVED; markAsRead is the dedicated transition to READ that simultaneously sets readAt, while updateStatus handles all other status transitions generically.
readAt is null until the notification is marked as read; once set it holds a timestamp and is never reset to null by any operation in this phase.

A Notification is always associated with a recipient (recipientId is non-null) and may optionally reference a related entity via relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId, both of which are nullable together.
NotificationStatus is a closed type alias with exactly four values — PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED — defined locally in the notification model file and not imported from shared types.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an empty array when no notifications exist for the recipient; never returns null. Results are ordered by creation time descending.

Always returns the newly created entity; the caller-provided data excludes id, createdAt, and readAt which are database-generated or default to null. A database failure propagates as a rejected promise.
Atomically sets read_at to NOW() and status to READ in a single UPDATE; returns the updated entity on success or null when no row matches the given id.

interfaceConstraints.operation: updateStatus(id: string, status: NotificationStatus): Promise<Notification | null>
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Performs a generic status transition to any NotificationStatus value; returns the updated entity on success or null when no row matches the given id.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: NotificationStatus must be defined as a local type alias in the notification model file, mirroring how BalanceStatus is defined locally in balance.model.ts rather than imported from shared types.

The NotificationRepository must follow the same repository implementation pattern as BalanceRepository: import pool from the shared db connection, use parameterized INSERT/UPDATE ... RETURNING * queries, and implement a private mapRow helper typed as Record<string, unknown> that converts snake_case columns to camelCase entity fields.

The notification barrel export must follow the same structure as the balance barrel: re-export the entity interface, the locally-defined status type, the repository interface, and the concrete repository class from their respective files.

Unit tests must follow the established test pattern: jest.mock the shared db connection module, assert exact SQL strings and exact parameter arrays via expect(mockQuery).toHaveBeenCalledWith(sql, params), and use a snake_case makeRow helper for mock row construction.
The repository must import the pool from the shared db connection module (which exports a pg.Pool instance named pool), matching how all existing repositories obtain their database connection.

The Notification entity shape must match the reconciled architecture's Notification domain entity attributes exactly — notably omitting updatedAt (the notifications table has no updated_at column) and including readAt as a nullable Date, distinguishing it from Employee/Policy/Leave/Balance which all carry updatedAt.

integrationPoints.why: The NotificationRepository depends on the exported pg Pool instance for all database access, matching the established pattern across employee/policy/leave/balance repositories.

The notification module depends on the shared types foundation from Phase 1; NotificationStatus is defined locally (not exported from shared types) following the BalanceStatus precedent, but the module's barrel must be consumable alongside other modules that import from shared types.

The leave service will depend on INotificationRepository to create notifications for managers and employees on leave lifecycle events (submission, approval, rejection, cancellation); this phase provides the repository interface and implementation that the leave service will consume.
